findings.text: the sibling temporary is opened with the caller's mode passed to os.open, whose mode the umask filters, so a caller asking for 0o600 can land 0o400: the pre-migration _write_private_json called os.chmod(temporary, 0o600) and its own comment at reckon/_backends.py:2096 states that a stricter umask must not leave the file below the mode the caller asked for, and the divergence reproduces under umask 277 as base 0o600 against head 0o400 while umask 022 and 077 agree.

assert mode == 0o640 encodes the ambient umask of the host that recorded it, so the assertion fails under umask 077 with 384 != 416 and holds only where the umask leaves 0o640 intact; _process_default_mode at :69 shows the derivation the same file already uses for its mode=None cases.

failure_attribution is empty and follow_ons is empty while the head arm exits 1 with 11 failures in the existing test files of touched modules (tests/test_backends.py, tests/test_capabilities.py, tests/test_crew_placement.py, tests/test_crew_lane_agnostic_placement.py), so the done-when's exit-0 clause is unmet and a reader cannot tell pre-existing from caused without recomputing the arm delta by hand.

measurement_module holds the path of the measuring script rather than the absolute __file__ of the module under test as imported, which is what the manifest contract asks for, and measure_writers.py prints no module.__file__ at all, so the identity of the tree the base arm measured is recoverable only from baseline_suite.command's PYTHONPATH; line 29 carries two working directories in prose rather than the one resolved directory the key asks for.

the gate log opens on the pytest progress line and names neither its revision, nor its tree, nor its command, so the log a later reader is handed cannot be attributed on its own; the same defect was filed against r-20260928T215628176452-one-timestamp-parser's head arm, so its remedy belongs in the dispatch template rather than in this node.
